biography: Patric Derdaele, a name once whispered with promise in Belgian racing circles, now echoes with a tinge of 'what could have been.' Born in the shadow of the Zolder circuit, the roar of engines was Patric's lullaby. His karting career was meteoric, marked by a fearless aggression that saw him clinch the Belgian National Championship at just 16. The transition to single-seaters was less smooth. A disastrous stint in Formula Renault, plagued by mechanical failures and a growing reputation for recklessness, nearly ended his career before it began. He found a home, surprisingly, in GT racing, specifically with the Ultima GTR team. For a time, he showed flashes of brilliance, but consistency remained elusive. Now, at 35, Patric is battling to stay relevant, clinging to the hope that one last victory might reignite the spark.
drivingStyle: Derdaele's driving is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and aggressive corner entries, often pushing his Ultima GTR to its absolute limit. While this approach can lead to spectacular overtakes, it also makes him prone to errors, especially under pressure. Tire management is not his forte, and he tends to overdrive the car early in a stint, leaving him vulnerable in the closing laps. He struggles to adapt to changing track conditions, often sticking to his initial strategy even when it becomes clear it's not working.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their karting days. Dubois, known for his clinical precision, often criticized Derdaele's aggressive style, leading to several on-track clashes and heated exchanges off the track.

Moreau, a rising star in GT racing, publicly called out Derdaele for his defensive driving tactics during a crucial race at Spa, accusing him of deliberately blocking her to protect his teammate's position.

Van Camp, a veteran driver known for his consistency and tire conservation, has consistently outperformed Derdaele in endurance races, fueling a sense of frustration and resentment on Derdaele's part.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, knitted by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to a specific opera aria ('Nessun Dorma') on repeat in the hours leading up to a race.
Has a habit of meticulously cleaning his racing gloves before each session, regardless of how clean they already are.
famousQuote: "I don't drive to finish second. I drive to win, even if it means taking a few risks."
careerHighlight: Winning the Spa 24 Hours in 2015, a hard-fought victory that saw him battling through the field after an early pit stop penalty.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Zolder GT Championship race in 2018, a devastating blow in front of his home crowd.
